quote.text: You have no proof the car was looked after when it is time to sell it.

promise.text: Selling your car: how to present your service history

lines.text: A dated record shows a buyer how a car was looked after.
What to put on the page, what a record you kept yourself can and can't show, and how to print it.

eyebrow.text: How to put the page together

body.text: Check the glove box, your email for shop receipts and invoices, and your bank statements for garage names.
A shop that has serviced the car can usually print its own history if you ask.

eyebrow.text: How to put the page together

head.text: Write one line per job, oldest first: date, odometer, what was done, who did it.

body.text: Add the cost if you know it.
If you did a job yourself, write "Me" and what parts you used.

eyebrow.text: How to put the page together

body.text: Where you don't know, write "not recorded" instead of guessing a date.

eyebrow.text: How to put the page together

head.text: Put the receipts behind the page in the same order as the lines, so the buyer can check one against the other.

eyebrow.text: How to put the page together

head.text: Read the last line against your odometer today.

body.text: If the last service was long ago, add today's date and mileage at the bottom.

line.text: Every service you record is kept with its day, mileage, who did it and what it cost, and prints as a service record that says plainly it is your own.
